cards.b: Vena cava → right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → left atrium → left ventricle → aorta.

short.q: Describe the movements of the diaphragm and intercostal muscles when breathing in.
short.model: The diaphragm contracts and flattens and the intercostal muscles contract, lifting the ribs up and out, increasing chest volume.
points: Intercostals contract, ribs up and out

short.q: Calculate the minute ventilation of a runner with a tidal volume of 2,500 ml and breathing rate of 30 per minute.
Describe two differences between arteries and veins.
short.model: Arteries carry blood away from the heart with thick muscular walls at high pressure. Veins carry blood towards the heart, have thin walls and valves.

short.q: State the effect of exercise on tidal volume and on residual volume.
short.model: Tidal volume increases with exercise as breaths get deeper; residual volume stays about the same.

short.q: Explain why a trained athlete has a lower resting heart rate.
short.model: Training makes the heart larger and stronger, so stroke volume is higher. The heart can pump the same cardiac output with fewer beats.
points: Higher stroke volume so fewer beats needed
